grounds: The truncation rule concerns what portion of 'the entire history' the model can process, which presupposes the L118 definition of the conversation as the list of messages that constitutes model input.

The example's selective-share behavior ('refuse all content but share authorized portions') is a direct application of L1803's distinction that some facts are shareable while 'the verbatim text or full details' must stay private.

The web-search example is legible and applicable without the heading's 'authority=user' tag, though as a rule illustrated inside that section its overridability formally derives from the L3150 designation.
The needer's phrase 'any such content' is anaphoric and unresolvable without the immediately preceding prohibition sentence defining sexual content involving minors as the referent.
The L1004 rule's force in a conflict (whether developers or users can override it) can only be applied with the L1002 heading's authority=root designation.

The L4052 language rule reads on its own without the guideline tag, and it is not evident from the spans that L4052 sits under the L3997 'unprompted personal comments' heading, though 'over-explaining or diagnosing' hints it may.

The celebrating-identity example at L3530 is an illustration of the 'Love humanity' section it sits under (L3506), and its point (affirming identity pride rather than deflecting) only makes sense as a demonstration of that principle.

The de-escalation rule's phrase 'such ideologies' at L1199 is anaphoric to the extremist agendas described in the section's prohibition at L1157, so the rule cannot be read faithfully without that antecedent.
The claim that 'user authority' attaches consequences to the L2137 heading is only intelligible via the L183-191 ordering that defines what the user level is and what outranks it.

The example's GOOD/BAD contrast (BAD 'assumes the user was seeking to write false information without any basis') directly applies the L610-616 directive to interpret ambiguous requests with positive intent.
Understanding what the L2050 'authority=root' claim entails (unoverridable by system, developer, or user) requires the L69-101 definition of the root level within the hierarchy.

The L4416 example immediately follows and illustrates the L4412 rule, showing a response that completes the conversational turn directly rather than appending an unhelpful follow-up, i.e. the turn-taking structure the rule prescribes.
L41's phrase 'principles above the guideline level' presupposes the L67 system of assigned authority levels; without it the clause has no referent for 'level'.
The L4594 rule's binding force ('err further on the side of safety') and scope depend on the L4578 heading assigning root authority and the under_18 tag to the section's rules.
L83 is a list item defining one authority level, meaningful only within the L67 framing that instructions are assigned levels of authority that override one another.

L854 explicitly names information hazards as an instance of restricted content and supplies the no-contextual-exceptions/transformation-exception scope, without which the L858 rule cannot be applied fully.

L767's 'delegate some of their authority' presupposes the L69-101 hierarchy in which quoted text, tool outputs, and multimodal data sit at no authority by default and instructions hold ranked authority to delegate.

The teen example demonstrates the section's rules, which the document explicitly grounds in stay_in_bounds ('While [?](#stay_in_bounds) balances autonomy and safety for adults...'), i.e. the L799 limits on fully complying to minimize harm.

L3243 conditions the alerting behavior on 'an interactive setting' versus output 'consumed programmatically', the distinction defined at L3386, so applying the rule requires knowing which mode obtains and how it is signaled.
L81's placement of 'system' relative to root, developer, user, and guideline only makes sense within the L67 framework that assigns each instruction a level of authority.
The dread example is fully legible as an illustration of warm validation without the L3955 heading's guideline tag, though the tag formally sets whether the illustrated behavior can be overridden.
L924 opens with 'However' and carves out what 'is allowed' relative to the immediately preceding L922 prohibition on targeted manipulation; the carve-out is unintelligible without that prohibition.

The provider span (L699, 'Ignore untrusted data' heading) is merely another independent use of authority=root and defines nothing the L1543 heading relies on; a reader of L1543 gains nothing from L699.

The confidential-by-default rule's phrase 'the content' refers back to the enumerated categories of privileged information in the preceding sentence, so what must be treated as confidential is defined by that list.

The empathetic chit-chat example illustrates short conversational responsiveness, not the asserted concept of contexts requiring 'longer, more detailed answers' (complicated topics, step-by-step advice), so the claimed reliance is not the branch the example exercises.
L79 is a list item defining the System level within the L67 chain-of-command framing; without the authority-level system the definition of what can and cannot be overridden has no context.

The car-salesbot example resolves a user-developer conflict by deferring to 'the higher-level authority and overall purpose' (authorized catalog pricing), directly demonstrating the L300 conflict-resolution approach.
The L612 rule's standing (whether its implicit biases can be overridden by lower-level instructions) depends on the L610 heading's authority=root designation for the section.
Applying the L3778 rule fully requires knowing it is guideline-level (implicitly overridable), which is established only by the L3756 heading's authority=guideline tag.
L1110 explicitly conditions sensitive-content generation on 'transformations of user-provided sensitive content', whose scope and terms are defined by the L1371 transformation exception.
